comparisons.peer_summary: Gross margin as a percentage of net revenue increased to 49% in 2024 from 46% in 2023. This increase was primarily driven by a favorable shift in revenue mix towards higher Data Center and Client revenues, as well as lower Gaming revenue, which was partially offset by the impact of lower Embedded revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD report increased gross margins in fiscal year 2024 driven by a favorable shift in revenue mix towards high-growth Data Center segments. NVDA attributes its margin increase (from 56.9% to 72.7%) to Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions, while AMD attributes its increase (from 46% to 49%) to a favorable shift in revenue mix towards higher Data Center and Client revenues. Both companies highlight Data Center strength as a primary driver for margin expansion, though NVDA’s expansion was significantly more pronounced and also benefited from reduced inventory charges compared to the prior year.

comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AVGO discuss gross margin trends in fiscal 2024, but with divergent percentage outcomes despite similar absolute margin growth. In contrast, AVGO’s gross margin percentage decreased to 63% from 69%, primarily due to higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets from the VMware Merger, despite absolute gross margin dollars increasing due to VMware contributions. Both disclose that inventory-related factors (provisions/amortization) played a significant role in their respective margin profiles.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consolidated gross margin improved to 22% in 2024 from -9% in 2023, aided by increased average selling prices and manufacturing cost reductions, despite the prior year's inventory write-downs and lower costs from selling previously written-down inventory in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and MU cite inventory-related financial movements as key drivers of their fiscal 2024 gross margin performance, but with opposite effects. NVDA reports that lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue helped drive its gross margin increase. Conversely, MU attributes its 2024 margin improvement (from -9% to 22%) not only to ASPs and cost reductions but specifically to 'lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023,' indicating a recovery from the inventory write-down charges that had previously depressed margins. Both companies highlight the resolution or reduction of inventory headwinds as a factor in 2024 margin trends.
